title: 7.9 A 60Gb/s NRZ Burst-Mode CDR with Cross-Injection Locking and Flash Phase Detector Achieving 0.13ns Reconfiguration Time in 28nm CMOS
problem: Rapidly reconfigurable photonic switch networks operating at ns-scale require burst-mode clock and data recovery (BM-CDR) with sub-ns reconfiguration time, but prior injection-locking BM-CDRs suffer from poor jitter at higher data rates.
motivation: Reducing BM-CDR reconfiguration time from ~10ns to sub-ns increases photonic switch throughput by 50% and improves data-center network latency and energy efficiency in AI-centric environments.
method: A 60-gigabit-per-second burst-mode clock-and-data recovery circuit recovers timing from arriving data bursts using cross-injection-locking—a technique where oscillators stabilize each other to reduce jitter (unwanted timing variations). It combines this with a flash phase detector (a fast circuit using parallel comparators that measures timing offset between data and clock within 2 bit periods). Implemented in 28nm CMOS, it achieves 0.13 nanosecond reconfiguration time.
key_novelty: The key idea is using cross-injection-locking—where oscillators mutually stabilize each other's frequency—to suppress jitter (unwanted timing variations) in burst-mode clock and data recovery.
contributions: 0.13ns reconfiguration time (50× faster than prior work)
Flash phase detector with 2UI acquisition window
baselines: injection-locking BM-CDR (poor jitter at high rates)
primary_theme: Ultra-fast burst-mode CDR for photonic switches
